title: Sports injuries & prevention
examples: What is the difference between a warm-up and a cool-down?
If I sprain my ankle, what should I do immediately?
Are there specific stretches for different sports?

explain.say: Today we will learn about keeping your body safe when you play sports.
A warm-up gets your muscles ready for the hard work ahead.
Next we look at what to do right after an injury happens.
Rest means stopping the activity to let the injured area settle down.

items: Give the body time to heal

explain.say: Ice helps to reduce swelling and calm down the pain quickly.

items: Apply cold pack for short times

explain.say: In real life, if you fall off your bike, you must follow these steps.

items: Apply ice pack to the knee
Elevate the leg above heart level

faq.q: How long should I apply ice to an injury?
faq.a: You should apply ice for about fifteen minutes at a time. Do not leave it on for too long.
asks: How many minutes of ice is okay?
What is the best time for an ice pack?

faq.q: Does compression mean wrapping it tightly?
faq.a: Compression means wrapping it firmly but not so tight that it cuts off circulation. You want support, not numbness.
asks: How tight should the bandage be?
What is the goal of compression?

faq.q: Is it okay to play sport the next day after an injury?
faq.a: No, you must wait until the pain has significantly reduced. Always check with an adult or professional first.
asks: When can I return to sport?
How long is the recovery period?

faq.q: What is dynamic stretching versus static stretching?
faq.a: Dynamic stretching involves movement, like lunges, while static stretching involves holding a stretch still.
asks: Should I stretch before or after?
What is the difference in stretching types?

faq.q: What if the pain is very bad?
faq.a: If the pain is severe or you cannot move the area at all, you should seek medical attention right away. Do not wait.
asks: When should I see a doctor?
What is a sign of a serious injury?

facts: Warm-ups increase blood flow to the muscles before exercise.
RICE stands for Rest, Ice, Compression, and Elevation.
Dynamic stretching involves controlled movements, not holding positions.
Elevation helps drain excess fluid from the injured area.

quiz.say: Which action should be part of a warm-up routine?

options.show: Holding a hamstring stretch for two minutes
options.say: Holding a hamstring stretch for two minutes

options.show: Doing deep squats without warming up
options.say: Doing deep squats without warming up

quiz.why: Jogging in place increases your heart rate gradually, which is the purpose of a warm-up.

wrong.0: This is static stretching, which is better suited for cooling down, not warming up.
wrong.1: Lifting heavy weights without preparation can cause immediate muscle strain.
wrong.2: Deep squats require muscles to be warm to prevent tearing.

quiz.say: If you sprain your ankle, which RICE component helps reduce swelling?
quiz.why: Applying ice helps to constrict blood vessels and reduce inflammation around the injury.

wrong.0: Elevation helps, but ice provides the direct cooling effect needed for inflammation.
wrong.2: Compression helps support the area, but ice is the primary agent for reducing swelling.
wrong.3: Rest is necessary, but it does not actively reduce the swelling itself.

quiz.say: When performing a warm-up, the goal is to:

options.show: Stretch every single muscle group deeply
options.say: Stretch every single muscle group deeply

quiz.why: The entire warm-up process aims to transition the body from rest to activity safely.

wrong.0: Fitness is built over time; a warm-up is just preparation, not a workout.
wrong.1: Cooling down happens after the activity, not during the warm-up phase.
wrong.2: Deep stretching before activity can sometimes temporarily weaken muscles.
